supportedConfiguration.qualification: Private invocation is the documented function-target boundary. handleSchedule validates schedule metadata, not authorization by itself. The proposed function must have only the schedule trigger and no public routes/rewrites. This receipt does not claim live artifact or invocation validation.
supportedConfiguration.nodeFetchHandler: Node.js runtime supports export default { fetch(request) { return Response; } }; the standalone scheduled entry uses this documented adapter shape.

credentialBoundary.productionCosmos: Retain the current uier production managed identity with Data Contributor on comments and app only. No preview-container scope or worker-app Vercel federation is added.
credentialBoundary.productionBlob: Use the existing production screenshot Blob connection and configured screenshots container; no key was read or rotated for this inspection.
credentialBoundary.previewMaintenance: The planned cutover retains the separate GitHub worker identity for manually invoked privileged preview/legacy maintenance. It does not add that identity to the Vercel production project.
credentialBoundary.oidcContext: The native function must preserve per-request Vercel OIDC context; no request token may be stored in a global mutable environment variable.
credentialBoundary.runtimeGuard: The project does not expose Vercel system environment variables. UIER_DEPLOYMENT_ENV and known production container names are the explicit configuration guard; reject non-production VERCEL_ENV when present, without requiring it to exist. Azure still validates the production-only federated OIDC subject.

steps: Confirm review-notifications has the intended private target and five-minute expression.
Inspect schedule execution history and function logs for successful production runs; distinguish expected overlap skips from failed work.
Compare scheduled time, execution time and completion state across consecutive occurrences before claiming restored cadence.
verificationAfterDeployment.inspectCommand: pnpm dlx vercel@65.16.0 schedules inspect review-notifications --cwd /tmp/uier-schedules-readiness --environment production --namespace default --json

checks: Load the traced worker closure from an isolated directory without production environment variables.
Confirm the bundled entry exports default.fetch.
Send a synthetic POST without schedule metadata and require HTTP 400 before any worker execution.
isolatedWorkerVerification.qualification: This is local dependency/runtime-adapter validation, not a live Vercel invocation or proof of private access controls.

prebuiltCliDryRun.fixture: A credential-free three-file Build Output API artifact: config.json with the native review-notifications schedule; private worker .vc-config.json with schedule/v1beta trigger; trivial default.fetch Node handler. The existing linked project requires an empty apps/web directory to validate rootDirectory.
prebuiltCliDryRun.shaCheck: Every CLI-reported SHA-1 equals the independently computed digest of the unmodified local file. The CLI retains the native schedules and private trigger configuration as prebuilt deployment inputs.
prebuiltCliDryRun.qualification: The CLI documents --dry as no upload/deployment creation. This establishes artifact input preservation only, not remote schema acceptance or a live scheduler execution.
